verdicts.reading: Apple's 2011 unit share of PC shipments in the US (and in Western Europe) is twice its 2007 share; Gartner's own framing for the US was 6.1% in 2007 to over 12% by 2011.
verdicts.reason: D16 quantitative rule on the US measure. Forecast about 12.2% (2 x 6.1%). Actual 2011: IDC full year 10.73%; Gartner quarters 9.3%, 12.9% (Q3), 11.6% (Q4), annual level about 11%. Error vs forecast 10-14% of the actual (ratio 1.76x-1.82x vs 2.0x): outside the 10% hit band, inside 25%: partial. Western Europe not verified by either grader. Grader A error: its cited MacDailyNews page (2011-10-12) gives no Western Europe share; the 7.6% vs 5.7% figure is not on the page, so A's 'both regions about doubled' is unsupported. A also rounded an about-11% annual US level to 'within 10% of 12%', which holds only at the top of the range.

verdicts.reading: By end 2012, traffic generated by physical sensors is 20% of non-video internet traffic.
verdicts.reason: A public measure exists: Cisco VNI (May 2013) puts all machine-to-machine traffic, a superset of sensor traffic, at 0.5% of global IP traffic in 2012. Even if non-video traffic were only 40% of IP traffic, M2M would be at most about 1.25% of non-video traffic, an order of magnitude below 20%. An upper bound this far below the forecast settles the claim; it is not a proxy of another quantity (D23). Miss. Grader B's ungradable rested on Cisco VNI being unreachable; the 2013 Cisco release is reachable.

evidence.title: Cisco's Visual Networking Index Forecast Projects Nearly Half the World's Population Will Be Connected to the Internet by 2017
evidence.shows: M2M traffic 0.5% of global IP traffic in 2012 (197 PB), 3% by 2017; global IP traffic about 44 EB per month in 2012.

verdicts.reading: In the 2014 worldwide ranking of mobile handset vendors by units sold, three of the top five are Chinese. Dominant reading in 2012: full-year ranking of all mobile phones.
verdicts.reason: Full-year 2014 all mobile phones (Gartner, via Wikipedia table): Samsung 392.5M, Apple 191.4M, Microsoft 185.7M, Lenovo/Motorola 84.0M, LG 76.1M, then Huawei 70.5M: one Chinese vendor in the top five. Full-year 2014 smartphones: Samsung, Apple, Lenovo, Huawei, LG: two. Only the Q4 2014 smartphone quarter (Apple, Samsung, Lenovo, Huawei, Xiaomi) has three. Three Chinese vendors in the full-year top five came in 2015 (smartphones: Huawei 104.1M, Lenovo 72.7M, BBK 72.4M). Not met on the dominant measure in 2014; met on the year-end quarter of a sub-measure and on full-year smartphones one year late: partial, following the late-arrival practice both graders used for event claims. Grader A graded a single-quarter smartphone ranking, a narrower reading than 'handset vendors by year-end 2014'. Grader B reading error: it listed Huawei in the 2014 all-phone top five, but its own figures put LG (76.1M) above Huawei (70.5M), so the count is one, not two.

verdicts.reading: Through 2014 the number of economically priced cars fitted with automated driver assistance (e.g. autonomous emergency braking) increases. The source omits the amount, so the claim is graded on direction only.
verdicts.reason: A public measure of fitment exists: in Japan, where low-priced kei cars got low-cost AEB from 2012 (Daihatsu Smart Assist, Mazda SCBS), 41% of new passenger cars sold in 2014 had collision mitigation braking, up from launches in 2012. The direction stated is met by 2014: hit. Caveat: the Japanese figure counts fitment, not only standard fitment. Grader A's ungradable rested on not finding a series; the omitted amount leaves a direction claim, which is gradable. Grader B's citation of UNECE R131 is weak: that regulation covers heavy vehicles, not economy cars; its other evidence (sensor demand, Honda/Toyota announcements) is indirect.

evidence.shows: 41% of new passenger cars sold in Japan in 2014 had collision mitigation braking; Mazda SCBS and Daihatsu Smart Assist (kei cars) launched 2012.

verdicts.reading: By 2017 mobile commerce is 50% of US digital commerce revenue.
verdicts.reason: Public measures exist. Digital Commerce 360 / eMarketer put mobile at nearly 35% (34.5%) of US e-commerce sales in 2017; comScore put mobile at 21% of total digital commerce dollars in Q4 2016 (the year before). Estimates span 21-35%, a factor under 2 (D23); median about 28%; even the high estimate is 30% below 50%. Miss. Grader A's ungradable was a retrieval gap, not an absence of measures; A itself recalled about one third.

verdicts.reading: By 2022 most people in mature economies consume more false information than true information.
verdicts.reason: Measured consumption of false news in a mature economy exists: Allen et al. (2020), on a representative US panel of TV, desktop and mobile use, find fake news at 0.15% of the daily media diet and news overall at most 14.2%. For false information to exceed true for most people, the share would have to exceed half; the measured share is orders of magnitude lower, and no later study reports a share near that. Miss. Grader A's Reuters DNR evidence measures concern, not consumption, as A said; but the consumption measure exists, so ungradable does not apply. Data years precede 2022; the gap is too large for the vintage to change the verdict.

evidence.title: Allen et al., Evaluating the fake news problem at the scale of the information ecosystem, Science Advances
evidence.shows: Fake news 0.15% of Americans' daily media diet; news of any sort at most 14.2%.

verdicts.reading: By 2023, enrollment of chronically ill patients in AI-enhanced virtual care avoids 20 million US emergency department visits.
verdicts.reason: The claim states a value attributed to a technology (visits avoided due to AI-enhanced virtual care). Under D23 such an attributed value is ungradable unless a public source measures the attribution; none does (NHAMCS and CDC report total visits, not visits avoided by virtual care). Grader A graded total ED visits (130.0M in 2018, 155.4M in 2022), a different quantity: totals can rise while a counterfactual reduction occurs, so the rise does not establish a miss. A's figures are correct; the reading is the error.

evidence.shows: 155.4 million US ED visits in 2022: total visits, no attribution to virtual care (cited by grader A).

evidence.title: Gartner Unveils Top Predictions for IT Organizations and Users in 2019 and Beyond
evidence.shows: Claim as published: reduction attributed to AI-enhanced virtual care enrollment.

verdicts.reading: By 2023 about 30% of world news and video content is authenticated as real by blockchain (adoption reading; 'up to 30%' read as the forecast level, not as any amount up to 30%).
verdicts.reason: Graded as an adoption claim under D16 (below 5% = miss). The news industry's provenance effort converged on C2PA (founded with BBC, Microsoft, Adobe, and the New York Times' involvement), which secures provenance with hash codes and certified digital signatures, not a blockchain. Blockchain authentication of news stayed at pilot or single-outlet scale, which bounds the share far below 5% of world news and video. No survey gives a share, but adoption at this scale is evident from what was deployed, as for other D16 adoption calls; ungradable would require that no measure of the claim's state exists. Least certain call in this set on the ungradable boundary.

evidence.title: Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: C2PA stores a hash of the content in metadata secured with a certified digital signature; no blockchain.

evidence.title: Content Authenticity Initiative (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: No blockchain in the CAI/C2PA architecture; no adoption share for news given.

verdicts.reading: By 2024, in CEO surveys of large organizations, 30% of CEOs name content moderation of user-generated content as a top priority.
verdicts.reason: The claim names its own measure, a CEO survey. Gartner's 2024 CEO and senior executive survey (416 respondents) reports top business priorities with shares (growth 62%, then technology and workforce); content moderation is not among the reported priorities, so its share is well below 30%. Miss. The survey release itself returned 403 and the archive was blocked; the priority list is from search summaries cited by grader B. Grader A looked for the item and found it absent, which is evidence of a miss rather than of no measure.

evidence.shows: 2024 CEO survey top priorities: growth (62%), technology, workforce; content moderation not among them (page 403; via search summary).
